verdict.rationale: Weaviate's own docs describe native multi-tenancy in which each tenant gets a separate shard, data is isolated between tenants, and tenants can be auto-created. That covers the core isolation part of the story. Nothing in the evidence shows how cheaply tenants scale or what the tenant limits are. Missing for 10: documented tenant-count or scale limits, evidence of low per-tenant cost at high tenant counts (e.g. inactive-tenant offloading), independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can isolate many tenants cheaply using namespaces, partitions, or per-tenant collections with documented limits

citations.quote: Multi-tenancy provides data isolation. Each tenant is stored on a separate shard. Data stored in one tenant is not visible to another tenant.
To change this behavior so Weaviate creates a new tenant, set `autoTenantCreation` to `true`
